sanskrit: sa rājā vyathito vyaśvo vidhanur hatasārathiḥ gadām ādāya kaunteyam abhidudrāva vegavān
english: Shaken, his horses gone, his bow broken, his charioteer slain, that king snatched up his mace and rushed swiftly upon the son of Kuntī.

sanskrit: tasyāpatata evāśu gadāṃ hemapariṣkṛtām śaraiś cakarta bahudhā bahubhir gṛdhravājitaiḥ
english: As he came charging, Arjuna at once cut his gold-adorned mace into many pieces with a host of vulture-feathered shafts.

sanskrit: sā gadā śakalībhūtā viśīrṇamaṇibandhanā vyālī nirmucyamāneva papātāsya sahasradhā
english: That mace, shattered into fragments, its jeweled mountings broken loose, fell in a thousand pieces, like a serpent sloughing off its skin.

sanskrit: virathaṃ taṃ vidhanvānaṃ gadayā parivarjitam naicchat tāḍayituṃ dhīmān arjunaḥ samarāgraṇīḥ
english: Chariotless, bowless, stripped now even of his mace—the wise Arjuna, foremost in battle, did not wish to strike him.

sanskrit: tata enaṃ vimanasaṃ kṣatradharme samāsthitam sāntvapūrvam idaṃ vākyam abravīt kapiketanaḥ
english: Then to him, downcast yet steadfast in the warrior's duty, the hero whose banner bore the ape spoke these gentle words.

sanskrit: paryāptaḥ kṣatradharmo 'yaṃ darśitaḥ putra gamyatām bahv etat samare karma tava bālasya pārthiva
english: "Enough—you have shown the warrior's code in full, my son. Go now. Great is this deed of yours in battle, O king, young as you are."

sanskrit: yudhiṣṭhirasya saṃdeśo na hantavyā nṛpā iti tena jīvasi rājaṃs tvam aparāddho 'pi me raṇe
english: "Yudhiṣṭhira's command is that kings are not to be slain. By that order you live, O king, though you offended me in the fight."

sanskrit: iti matvā sa cātmānaṃ pratyādiṣṭaṃ sma māgadhaḥ tathyam ity avagamyainaṃ prāñjaliḥ pratyapūjayat
english: The Māgadha king, understanding himself thus dismissed and knowing the words to be true, with joined palms paid him honor in return.

sanskrit: tam arjunaḥ samāśvāsya punar evedam abravīt āgantavyaṃ parāṃ caitrīm aśvamedhe nṛpasya naḥ
english: Arjuna reassured him and spoke again: "You must come at the next full moon of Caitra, to our king's horse-sacrifice."

sanskrit: ity uktaḥ sa tathety uktvā pūjayām āsa taṃ hayam phalgunaṃ ca yudhāṃ śreṣṭhaṃ vidhivat sahadevajaḥ
english: Thus addressed, the son of Sahadeva said "So be it," and duly did honor both to the horse and to Phalguna, the best of warriors.

sanskrit: tato yatheṣṭam agamat punar eva sa kesarī tataḥ samudratīreṇa vaṅgān puṇḍrān sakeralān
english: Then once more the maned steed roamed where it pleased, going along the seacoast to the Vaṅgas, the Puṇḍras, and the Keralas.

sanskrit: tatra tatra ca bhūrīṇi mlecchasainyāny anekaśaḥ vijigye dhanuṣā rājan gāṇḍīvena dhanaṃjayaḥ
english: And there, O king, in place after place, Dhanaṃjaya conquered with his bow Gāṇḍīva the many great hosts of the Mlecchas.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca māgadhenārcito rājan pāṇḍavaḥ śvetavāhanaḥ dakṣiṇāṃ diśam āsthāya cārayām āsa taṃ hayam
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: Honored by the Māgadha king, O sovereign, the Pāṇḍava of the white steeds turned to the southern quarter and let the horse range on.

sanskrit: tataḥ sa punar āvṛtya hayaḥ kāmacaro balī āsasāda purīṃ ramyāṃ cedīnāṃ śuktisāhvayām
english: Then the strong horse, wandering at its will, turned back and reached the lovely city of the Cedis, called Śuktimatī.

sanskrit: śarabheṇārcitas tatra śiśupālātmajena saḥ yuddhapūrveṇa mānena pūjayā ca mahābalaḥ
english: There the mighty hero was honored by Śarabha, son of Śiśupāla, with respect and homage preceded by a token fight.

sanskrit: tatrārcito yayau rājaṃs tadā sa turagottamaḥ kāśīn andhrān kosalāṃś ca kirātān atha taṅgaṇān
english: Honored there, O king, that finest of horses then went on to the Kāśis, the Andhras, the Kosalas, the Kirātas, and the Taṅgaṇas.

sanskrit: tatra pūjāṃ yathānyāyaṃ pratigṛhya sa pāṇḍavaḥ punar āvṛtya kaunteyo daśārṇān agamat tadā
english: There the Pāṇḍava received their homage as was due, and the son of Kuntī turned again and came to the Daśārṇas.

sanskrit: tatra citrāṅgado nāma balavān vasudhādhipaḥ tena yuddham abhūt tasya vijayasyātibhairavam
english: There a mighty lord of the earth named Citrāṅgada gave Vijaya a most terrible battle.

sanskrit: taṃ cāpi vaśam ānīya kirīṭī puruṣarṣabhaḥ niṣādarājño viṣayam ekalavyasya jagmivān
english: Having brought him too to submission, the diademed bull among men passed into the realm of Ekalavya, king of the Niṣādas.

sanskrit: ekalavyasutaś cainaṃ yuddhena jagṛhe tadā tataś cakre niṣādaiḥ sa saṃgrāmaṃ romaharṣaṇam
english: And Ekalavya's son confronted him then in battle, and he waged with the Niṣādas a fight that made the hair stand on end.

sanskrit: tatas tam api kaunteyaḥ samareṣv aparājitaḥ jigāya samare vīro yajñavighnārtham udyatam
english: Then the son of Kuntī, unvanquished in battles, the hero conquered him too in combat, risen up to hinder the sacrifice.

sanskrit: sa taṃ jitvā mahārāja naiṣādiṃ pākaśāsaniḥ arcitaḥ prayayau bhūyo dakṣiṇaṃ salilārṇavam
english: Having conquered the son of the Niṣāda, O great king, the offspring of Indra, the chastiser of Pāka, was honored and went on once more toward the southern ocean.

sanskrit: tatrāpi draviḍair andhrai raudrair māhiṣakair api tathā kollagireyaiś ca yuddham āsīt kirīṭinaḥ
english: There too the diademed one had battle with the Draviḍas, the Andhras, the fierce Māhiṣakas, and the people of Kollagiri.

sanskrit: turagasya vaśenātha surāṣṭrān abhito yayau gokarṇam api cāsādya prabhāsam api jagmivān
english: Then, following the horse's lead, he went on toward the Surāṣṭras, reached Gokarṇa, and came also to Prabhāsa.

sanskrit: tato dvāravatīṃ ramyāṃ vṛṣṇivīrābhirakṣitām āsasāda hayaḥ śrīmān kururājasya yajñiyaḥ
english: Then the splendid sacrificial horse of the Kuru king reached lovely Dvāravatī, guarded by the heroes of the Vṛṣṇis.

sanskrit: tam unmathya hayaśreṣṭhaṃ yādavānāṃ kumārakāḥ prayayus tāṃs tadā rājann ugraseno nyavārayat
english: The young princes of the Yādavas, harrying that best of horses, set out against it, but Ugrasena, O king, held them back.

sanskrit: tataḥ puryā viniṣkramya vṛṣṇyandhakapatis tadā sahito vasudevena mātulena kirīṭinaḥ
english: Then the lord of the Vṛṣṇis and Andhakas came forth from the city, together with Vasudeva, the maternal uncle of the diademed hero.

sanskrit: tau sametya kuruśreṣṭhaṃ vidhivat prītipūrvakam parayā bharataśreṣṭhaṃ pūjayā samavasthitau tatas tābhyām anujñāto yayau yena hayo gataḥ
english: The two came up to the foremost of the Kurus and stood ready to honor that best of the Bharatas duly and with affection, with the highest homage; then, taking leave of them, he went on by the way the horse had gone.

sanskrit: tataḥ sa paścimaṃ deśaṃ samudrasya tadā hayaḥ krameṇa vyacarat sphītaṃ tataḥ pañcanadaṃ yayau
english: Then the horse roamed in turn through the prosperous western country of the sea, and from there it came to the land of the Five Rivers.

sanskrit: tasmād api sa kauravya gāndhāraviṣayaṃ hayaḥ vicacāra yathākāmaṃ kaunteyānugatas tadā
english: And from there, O Kaurava, the horse wandered at its will into the realm of the Gāndhāras, followed all the while by the son of Kuntī.

sanskrit: tatra gāndhārarājena yuddham āsīn mahātmanaḥ ghoraṃ śakuniputreṇa pūrvavairānusāriṇā
english: There the great-souled one had a fearful battle with the king of the Gāndhāras, the son of Śakuni, who pursued the old enmity.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca śakunes tu suto vīro gāndhārāṇāṃ mahārathaḥ pratyudyayau guḍākeśaṃ sainyena mahatā vṛtaḥ hastyaśvarathapūrṇena patākādhvajamālinā
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: The valiant son of Śakuni, great chariot-warrior of the Gāndhāras, advanced against Guḍākeśa, surrounded by a vast army full of elephants, horses, and chariots and garlanded with banners and flags.

sanskrit: amṛṣyamāṇās te yodhā nṛpateḥ śakuner vadham abhyayuḥ sahitāḥ pārthaṃ pragṛhītaśarāsanāḥ
english: Those warriors, unable to bear the slaying of King Śakuni, advanced together upon Pārtha with bows drawn.

sanskrit: tān uvāca sa dharmātmā bībhatsur aparājitaḥ yudhiṣṭhirasya vacanaṃ na ca te jagṛhur hitam
english: To them the righteous and unvanquished Bībhatsu spoke Yudhiṣṭhira's words, but they would not heed his wholesome counsel.

sanskrit: vāryamāṇās tu pārthena sāntvapūrvam amarṣitāḥ parivārya hayaṃ jagmus tataś cukrodha pāṇḍavaḥ
english: Though restrained by Pārtha with conciliating words, the enraged men surrounded the horse and seized it; thereupon the Pāṇḍava grew wrathful.

sanskrit: tataḥ śirāṃsi dīptāgrais teṣāṃ ciccheda pāṇḍavaḥ kṣurair gāṇḍīvanirmuktair nātiyatnād ivārjunaḥ
english: Then with flame-tipped razor-shafts loosed from Gāṇḍīva, Arjuna the Pāṇḍava cut off their heads as if with scarcely any effort.

sanskrit: te vadhyamānāḥ pārthena hayam utsṛjya saṃbhramāt nyavartanta mahārāja śaravarṣārditā bhṛśam
english: Cut down by Pārtha, they let go the horse in their panic and turned back, O great king, sorely tormented by the rain of arrows.

sanskrit: vitudyamānas taiś cāpi gāndhāraiḥ pāṇḍavarṣabhaḥ ādiśyādiśya tejasvī śirāṃsy eṣāṃ nyapātayat
english: Though harassed by those Gāndhāras, the lustrous bull of the Pāṇḍavas, marking each man out one by one, sent their heads tumbling down.

sanskrit: vadhyamāneṣu teṣv ājau gāndhāreṣu samantataḥ sa rājā śakuneḥ putraḥ pāṇḍavaṃ pratyavārayat
english: As the Gāndhāras were being slain on every side in the fray, that king, the son of Śakuni, moved to check the Pāṇḍava.

sanskrit: taṃ yudhyamānaṃ rājānaṃ kṣatradharme vyavasthitam pārtho 'bravīn na me vadhyā rājāno rājaśāsanāt alaṃ yuddhena te vīra na te 'sty adya parājayaḥ
english: To that king as he fought, steadfast in the warrior's duty, Pārtha said: "Kings are not to be slain by me, by the king's command. Enough of fighting, O hero—there is no defeat for you this day."

sanskrit: ity uktas tad anādṛtya vākyam ajñānamohitaḥ sa śakrasamakarmāṇam avākirata sāyakaiḥ
english: Thus addressed, he slighted those words, deluded by ignorance, and showered with arrows the one whose deeds equaled Śakra's.

sanskrit: tasya pārthaḥ śirastrāṇam ardhacandreṇa patriṇā apāharad asaṃbhrānto jayadrathaśiro yathā
english: Calmly, with a crescent-headed feathered shaft, Pārtha swept away his helmet, as once he had taken the head of Jayadratha.

sanskrit: tad dṛṣṭvā vismayaṃ jagmur gāndhārāḥ sarva eva te icchatā tena na hato rājety api ca te viduḥ
english: Seeing this, all the Gāndhāras were filled with wonder, and they understood that the king had not been slain only because Arjuna so willed.

sanskrit: gāndhārarājaputras tu palāyanakṛtakṣaṇaḥ babhau tair eva sahitas trastaiḥ kṣudramṛgair iva
english: But the son of the Gāndhāra king, intent upon flight, looked, together with those frightened men, like a small beast among the timid creatures.

sanskrit: teṣāṃ tu tarasā pārthas tatraiva paridhāvatām vijahārottamāṅgāni bhallaiḥ saṃnataparvabhiḥ
english: As they scattered swiftly about that very field, Pārtha struck off their heads with broad-bladed shafts well-jointed at the bend.

sanskrit: ucchritāṃs tu bhujān ke cin nābudhyanta śarair hṛtān śarair gāṇḍīvanirmuktaiḥ pṛthubhiḥ pārthacoditaiḥ
english: Some did not even feel their upraised arms carried away by the broad arrows loosed from Gāṇḍīva and sped by Pārtha.

sanskrit: saṃbhrāntanaranāgāśvam atha tad vidrutaṃ balam hatavidhvastabhūyiṣṭham āvartata muhur muhuḥ
english: Then that host, its men, elephants, and horses thrown into confusion, broke and fled, most of it slain and shattered, wheeling about again and again.

sanskrit: na hy adṛśyanta vīrasya ke cid agre 'gryakarmaṇaḥ ripavaḥ pātyamānā vai ye saheyur mahāśarān
english: For not one of the foes, struck down before that hero of foremost deeds, could be seen to withstand his mighty arrows.

sanskrit: tato gāndhārarājasya mantrivṛddhapuraḥsarā jananī niryayau bhītā puraskṛtyārghyam uttamam
english: Then the mother of the Gāndhāra king, led by aged ministers, came forth in fear, bearing before her the choicest offering of welcome.

sanskrit: sā nyavārayad avyagrā taṃ putraṃ yuddhadurmadam prasādayām āsa ca taṃ jiṣṇum akliṣṭakāriṇam
english: Composed, she restrained her son, mad with battle-frenzy, and she sought to appease the victorious one of untiring deeds.

sanskrit: tāṃ pūjayitvā kaunteyaḥ prasādam akarot tadā śakuneś cāpi tanayaṃ sāntvayann idam abravīt
english: The son of Kuntī honored her and then granted his grace, and soothing the son of Śakuni too he spoke thus.

sanskrit: na me priyaṃ mahābāho yat te buddhir iyaṃ kṛtā pratiyoddhum amitraghna bhrātaiva tvaṃ mamānagha
english: "It does not please me, O mighty-armed slayer of foes, that you set your mind to fight against me; you are a brother to me, O sinless one."

sanskrit: gāndhārīṃ mātaraṃ smṛtvā dhṛtarāṣṭrakṛtena ca tena jīvasi rājaṃs tvaṃ nihatās tv anugās tava
english: "Remembering my mother Gāndhārī, and for Dhṛtarāṣṭra's sake—by that you live, O king, though your followers are slain."

sanskrit: maivaṃ bhūḥ śāmyatāṃ vairaṃ mā te bhūd buddhir īdṛśī āgantavyaṃ parāṃ caitrīm aśvamedhe nṛpasya naḥ
english: "Be not thus; let the enmity be quelled; let your mind no longer be of this sort. You must come at the next full moon of Caitra, to our king's horse-sacrifice."

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca ity uktvānuyayau pārtho hayaṃ taṃ kāmacāriṇam nyavartata tato vājī yena nāgāhvayaṃ puram
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: Having spoken thus, Pārtha followed the horse that wandered at its will, and then the steed turned back toward the city named for the elephant.

sanskrit: taṃ nivṛttaṃ tu śuśrāva cāreṇaiva yudhiṣṭhiraḥ śrutvārjunaṃ kuśalinaṃ sa ca hṛṣṭamanābhavat
english: Yudhiṣṭhira learned through a spy that it had turned back, and on hearing that Arjuna was well he was glad at heart.

sanskrit: vijayasya ca tat karma gāndhāraviṣaye tadā śrutvānyeṣu ca deśeṣu sa suprīto 'bhavan nṛpaḥ
english: And hearing of Vijaya's deeds in the realm of the Gāndhāras and in the other lands, the king was greatly pleased.

sanskrit: etasminn eva kāle tu dvādaśīṃ māghapākṣikīm iṣṭaṃ gṛhītvā nakṣatraṃ dharmarājo yudhiṣṭhiraḥ
english: At that very season the Dharma King Yudhiṣṭhira chose the twelfth day of the fortnight of Māgha and a favorable lunar mansion.

sanskrit: samānāyya mahātejāḥ sarvān bhrātṝn mahāmanāḥ bhīmaṃ ca nakulaṃ caiva sahadevaṃ ca kauravaḥ
english: The greatly lustrous, high-minded Kaurava summoned all his brothers together—Bhīma, and Nakula, and Sahadeva.

sanskrit: provācedaṃ vacaḥ kāle tadā dharmabhṛtāṃ varaḥ āmantrya vadatāṃ śreṣṭho bhīmaṃ bhīmaparākramam
english: Then in due time that best of the upholders of dharma, the foremost of speakers, addressing Bhīma of terrible prowess, spoke these words.

sanskrit: āyāti bhīmasenāsau sahāśvena tavānujaḥ yathā me puruṣāḥ prāhur ye dhanaṃjayasāriṇaḥ
english: "Bhīmasena, your younger brother is coming with the horse, as the men told me who followed in Dhanaṃjaya's track."

sanskrit: upasthitaś ca kālo 'yam abhito vartate hayaḥ māghī ca paurṇamāsīyaṃ māsaḥ śeṣo vṛkodara
english: "The time has come, and the horse is near at hand; the full moon of Māgha approaches, and but a month remains, O Vṛkodara."

sanskrit: tat prasthāpyantu vidvāṃso brāhmaṇā vedapāragāḥ vājimedhārthasiddhyarthaṃ deśaṃ paśyantu yajñiyam
english: "So let learned Brahmins, masters of the Vedas, be sent forth; for the accomplishment of the horse-sacrifice let them survey a fit ground."

sanskrit: ity uktaḥ sa tu tac cakre bhīmo nṛpatiśāsanam hṛṣṭaḥ śrutvā narapater āyāntaṃ savyasācinam
english: Thus addressed, Bhīma carried out the king's command, rejoicing to hear from his sovereign that Savyasācin was returning.

sanskrit: tato yayau bhīmasenaḥ prājñaiḥ sthapatibhiḥ saha brāhmaṇān agrataḥ kṛtvā kuśalān yajñakarmasu
english: Then Bhīmasena set out with skilled master-builders, placing at their head Brahmins versed in the rites of sacrifice.

sanskrit: taṃ saśālacayagrāmaṃ saṃpratolīviṭaṅkinam māpayām āsa kauravyo yajñavāṭaṃ yathāvidhi
english: The Kaurava had measured out the sacrificial enclosure according to rule, with its rows of halls and dwellings, its broad streets and turreted gateways.

sanskrit: sadaḥ sapatnīsadanaṃ sāgnīdhram api cottaram kārayām āsa vidhivan maṇihemavibhūṣitam
english: He had built, duly and adorned with gems and gold, the assembly hall, the queens' pavilion, and beyond it the chamber of the fire-priest.

sanskrit: stambhān kanakacitrāṃś ca toraṇāni bṛhanti ca yajñāyatanadeśeṣu dattvā śuddhaṃ ca kāñcanam
english: He set up pillars bright with gold and lofty archways throughout the precincts of the sacrificial site, bestowing pure gold as well.

sanskrit: antaḥpurāṇi rājñāṃ ca nānādeśanivāsinām kārayām āsa dharmātmā tatra tatra yathāvidhi
english: And the righteous one had inner apartments built, each in its place as was fitting, for the kings dwelling in their various lands.

sanskrit: brāhmaṇānāṃ ca veśmāni nānādeśasameyuṣām kārayām āsa bhīmaḥ sa vividhāni hy anekaśaḥ
english: And for the Brahmins who had gathered from many lands, Bhīma had dwellings built, varied and manifold.

sanskrit: tathā saṃpreṣayām āsa dūtān nṛpatiśāsanāt bhīmaseno mahārāja rājñām akliṣṭakarmaṇām
english: Likewise, O great king, by the sovereign's order Bhīmasena dispatched envoys to the kings of untiring deeds.

sanskrit: te priyārthaṃ kurupater āyayur nṛpasattamāḥ ratnāny anekāny ādāya striyo 'śvān āyudhāni ca
english: To please the lord of the Kurus those best of kings came, bringing many jewels, women, horses, and weapons.

sanskrit: teṣāṃ niviśatāṃ teṣu śibireṣu sahasraśaḥ nardataḥ sāgarasyeva śabdo divam ivāspṛśat
english: As they settled by the thousands in those encampments, the tumult, like the roaring of the sea, seemed to touch the heavens.

sanskrit: teṣām abhyāgatānāṃ sa rājā rājīvalocanaḥ vyādideśānnapānāni śayyāś cāpy atimānuṣāḥ
english: For those who had come, the lotus-eyed king ordered food and drink and couches of more than human splendor.

sanskrit: vāhanānāṃ ca vividhāḥ śālāḥ śālīkṣugorasaiḥ upetāḥ puruṣavyāghra vyādideśa sa dharmarāṭ
english: And for the draught animals the Dharma King ordered manifold stalls, furnished with rice, sugarcane, and milk, O tiger among men.

sanskrit: tathā tasmin mahāyajñe dharmarājasya dhīmataḥ samājagmur munigaṇā bahavo brahmavādinaḥ
english: And at that great sacrifice of the wise Dharma King many bands of sages, expounders of the sacred word, assembled.

sanskrit: ye ca dvijātipravarās tatrāsan pṛthivīpate samājagmuḥ saśiṣyāṃs tān pratijagrāha kauravaḥ
english: And the most eminent of the twice-born who were there, O lord of the earth, gathered together with their disciples, and the Kaurava received them.

sanskrit: sarvāṃś ca tān anuyayau yāvad āvasathād iti svayam eva mahātejā dambhaṃ tyaktvā yudhiṣṭhiraḥ
english: And the greatly lustrous Yudhiṣṭhira himself, casting off all pride, accompanied each of them as far as his lodging.

sanskrit: tataḥ kṛtvā sthapatayaḥ śilpino 'nye ca ye tadā kṛtsnaṃ yajñavidhiṃ rājan dharmarājñe nyavedayan
english: Then the master-builders and the other craftsmen, having completed the whole apparatus of the sacrifice, reported it, O king, to the Dharma King.

sanskrit: tac chrutvā dharmarājaḥ sa kṛtaṃ sarvam aninditam hṛṣṭarūpo 'bhavad rājā saha bhrātṛbhir acyutaḥ
english: Hearing that all had been done faultlessly, the Dharma King, that steadfast sovereign, grew joyful in form together with his brothers.
